decision: CheMeleon is loaded from a LOCAL foundation file holding its own weights widened by two zero-initialised atom-feature columns. DEPARTS FROM THE BRIEF, which assumed `--atom-features-path` was available with CheMeleon.
why: chemprop 2.3.1 refuses --atom-features-path outright when CheMeleon is named (cli/train.py, 'CheMeleon does not support passing --atom-features-path'), confirmed by a real CLI call in Part 0.2, because its published W_i is (2048, 86) against a 72-wide V2 atom featurizer. The brief names CheMeleon AND per-atom features and those are mutually exclusive through the documented route. The local path skips that validation and takes only message_passing and agg from the file, so the surgery preserves the pretrained encoder exactly: at init the widened block reproduces CheMeleon to 0.0 on a real molecule with random extra feature values, and the only new parameters are the two zero columns.
alternative: Drop CheMeleon and use a random-init chemprop, which supports the flag. That would have moved the baseline off `plain` -- this project's best single model and the arm notebook 37 stored on these exact folds -- onto chemprop_randominit, answering a weaker question. Or abandon the per-atom half, which is the entire bet, leaving a re-run of notebook 44's null.

decision: --no-atom-feature-scaling is passed and the per-atom values are standardised in scripts/52_atom_arrays.py instead, from each fold's screen_inner_train atoms.
why: On the --from-foundation path chemprop computes the atom-feature scaler and LOGS it but never attaches the GraphTransform to the loaded encoder (Part 0.4b: the foundation branch contains no graph_transform assignment; the non-foundation branch does). normalize_inputs mutates the training arrays in place, so training is scaled and the checkpoint carries nn.Identity -- predict would feed the same features UNSCALED. Demonstrated on two real checkpoints, not inferred. Left alone this would be a silent train/predict mismatch on every blind prediction.
alternative: Let chemprop scale and accept the mismatch, which would corrupt stage 2's submission invisibly. Or patch the installed chemprop, which this project does not do to vendored dependencies.

decision: The wiring control is an all-ZEROS npz rather than dropping the flag.
why: Dropping the flag would also change the encoder and the command line, so a difference could come from anywhere. Holding everything fixed but the npz CONTENTS means a non-zero difference can only be the values having reached the model.
alternative: Fit plain CheMeleon as the control, which is what the brief's wording suggests. It answers a looser question and cannot isolate the wiring.

decision: PROCESS NOTE, not a design choice: the wiring check was run three times because I corrupted the first attempt myself.
why: The first driver was launched with `nohup ... &` inside a foreground shell call. When that call returned, a single `pgrep` on the DRIVER's own command line came back empty and I concluded the run was dead -- but the pattern never matched the `chemprop` CHILD, which was alive and still training. Acting on that reading I deleted the run directory under a live process and started a second driver on the same paths; the two collided inside Lightning's CSVLogger (`ValueError: dict contains fields not in fieldnames`) and the second crashed while the first carried on into a deleted directory. Both were killed, every partial artefact was removed, and the check was re-run as a single harness-tracked job. Same class as notebook 30's nbformat/nbconvert race: two processes, one set of files. The lesson is to check for the CHILD process, not just the driver, and never to delete a run directory on the strength of one liveness probe.
alternative: None -- this is recorded because it happened, not because it was chosen. No result in this notebook comes from the corrupted attempts; the run directory was emptied before the surviving run started.

decision: STAGE 1a: heavy atoms with no attached hydrogen are filled with 0.0 in min_attached_H_charge. 45.1% of heavy atoms, so not a corner case.
why: Four pieces of evidence, none of them preference. (1) It is chemprop's own convention: MoleculeDatapoint sets NAN_TOKEN = 0 and fills V_f's NaNs with it, so passing NaN produces exactly 0.0. (2) It cannot create a confound, because the V2 featurizer already one-hot encodes total_num_Hs (verified on a real molecule), so the model can distinguish a no-hydrogen atom independently; the fill can distort a scale but cannot hide a distinction. (3) Attached-hydrogen charges run -0.0027 to 0.2033 with p1 at 0.0092, so 0.0 sits at the extreme low edge and reads as 'no hydrogen-borne positive charge', which is literally true -- with 7 of 113,596 hydrogens at or below 0, stated rather than rounded to none. (4) Measured: at 0.0 the has-H split takes 44.9% of the column's variance, leaving 55% genuine within-group variation; at -1.0 it takes 99.8% and the column becomes a has-H indicator in disguise, which is the sentinel failure mode notebook 45 documented.
alternative: A far sentinel (-1.0), which measurement rules out; or mean-imputation, which erases the distinction entirely (0.0% between-group).

decision: STAGE 1a: no second full wiring fit was run after adding the third column.
why: The mechanism is unchanged -- one more column through the same path -- and the two things that could break were checked directly instead: the k=3 widened encoder reproduces CheMeleon to 0.0 at init, and the foundation file is named by k with its own d_v asserted on load so a stale k=2 file cannot be reused. Stage 1b's control re-tests the zeroed case at 5 folds in any event.
alternative: Repeat the two-fit wiring check at k=3, about 30 min, to re-measure a quantity whose mechanism had not changed.

decision: The scaler is fitted on screen_inner_train only, not on the pooled train+val rows.
why: That is the population chemprop's own scaler uses (train_dset.normalize_inputs, with val_dset given the fitted scaler), so the arm matches what every other chemprop arm in this project effectively did for its molecule-level descriptors, and the early-stopping set stays outside the statistics.
alternative: Fit on pooled train+val. Marginally more data for the statistics, at the cost of a quantity fitted partly on the set used to stop training.
